name: infra_tf_custom_loop
title: TensorFlow 2 custom training loop: tf.GradientTape + tf.function + MirroredStrategy, no model.fit()
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-infra: the TF shape that is not `.fit()`
note: A pure precision trap for the Keras and torch rule families at once: there is no compile(), no fit() and no callback list for MLV705 / MLV709 to read, and no torch anywhere for MLV2xx / MLV3xx to recommend. MLView reports nothing, which is correct. Three graph-side observations are recorded in stagesObserved and reported separately, and none of them is a finding, so none of them is labelled here.
stagesObserved: config, data, preprocess, model, objective, train and eval present; `deliver` reported ABSENT although tf.train.Checkpoint (141), tf.train.CheckpointManager (143), manager.save(checkpoint_number=epoch) (157) and model.export(...) (162) are all present - none of the four is in analyzer/src/mlview/knowledge/tf_tbl.py and no diagnostic declares the gap (INFRA-R2-07). `workspace.frameworks` reads `torch, numpy, keras, tf` on a workspace with no torch import: `optimizer.apply_gradients(...)` at line 84 resolves to the fabricated FQN `torch.optim.Optimizer.apply_gradients` (INFRA-R2-06). The two batch loops at 151 and 154 draw no node at all, and main() itself is drawn as an `eval_loop` with the evaluation answer reading `Evaluation runs in main() at train.py:123` (INFRA-R2-05).

forbidden.why: nothing in this workspace fits a transformer; splits.standardize computes mean/std from the training half only and is not even called
standardize() takes x_train and x_val already split and derives its statistics from x_train alone
no fit / fit_transform call exists in this workspace
the cut is chronological_split() - a literal index slice - and nothing shuffles across it
there is no torch DataLoader in this workspace; the training pipeline shuffles with a 4096-element buffer at line 64
the validation pipeline at lines 67-69 is batch + prefetch with no shuffle
the holdout is cut by chronological_split at line 60, BEFORE tf.data sees a row; the shuffle at line 64 is applied to the training half only and no take()/skip() follows it
MLV301 is a torch rule and there is no torch model here; TensorFlow spells the mode switch training=False, which line 101 passes
MLV302 is a torch rule; torch.no_grad() does not exist in TensorFlow and the eval step is already outside any GradientTape
SparseCategoricalAccuracy takes logits by design - it argmaxes internally - so feeding it the raw head output at lines 87 and 102 is correct
the head at line 51 is Dense(classes) with no activation and the loss carries from_logits=True at line 138; that is the correct pairing
tf.random.set_seed(args.seed) at line 125 and keras.utils.set_random_seed(args.seed) at line 126, plus np.random.default_rng(seed) at line 56
there is no sklearn splitter and no random_split; the cut is a literal index and the shuffle at line 64 passes seed=seed
there is no model.fit() in this workspace, so the rule that requires compile() before fit() has nothing to judge
Dense(classes) at line 51 emits logits and from_logits=True at line 138 says so; the two agree
there is no torch.save and no torch.load anywhere; the checkpoint is a tf.train.CheckpointManager
